caption:
One ordinary day on Britain's railways: 22,264 scheduled train services, all moving at once.

Watch the network wake before dawn, saturate at rush hour and empty out overnight — every dot is a real service, from intercity to sleeper.

📊 See a full day of British rail traffic in this animated flow map, built from the published National Rail GTFS timetable for Thursday 3 September 2026, across 2,584 stations. Explore how London pulls the whole network, and when the country actually moves.

Source: National Rail GTFS via travelwhiz, data from RDG/ATOC (CC BY 4.0). Positions are interpolated between the published stops; stations are joined in straight lines, as the GTFS carries no track geometry. Service classes approximate the operator: intercity (Avanti, LNER, GWR, CrossCountry, TransPennine…), night (Caledonian Sleeper), regional (the rest).
